segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: They figured nothing's really going to go wrong. We need to switch over from copper to fiber, and we need to add a new router to support the new network capability.

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: And then shortly after that upgrade was made, they started to see that that we was sending out a lot of pings. There was also an issue that they noticed at a radar facility in Amarillo, Texas.

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: And this over-activity started basically like flooding the system. And so the officials looked at this, they saw these errant things happening, decided that they couldn't figure out how to shut it down quickly
segments.ko: 이러한 과잉 활동이 기본적으로 시스템을 마비시키기 시작했습니다. 관계자들은 이를 지켜보고 비정상적인 일이 벌어지는 것을 보았고, 빠르게 차단할 방법을 찾을 수 없다고 판단했습니다.

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: So to understand how this all works, you kind of need a basic map of how the air traffic control network is laid out. There are a number of different components.
segments.ko: 이 모든 게 어떻게 돌아가는지 이해하려면 항공 교통 관제 네트워크가 어떻게 배치되어 있는지 기초적인 지도가 필요합니다. 여러 가지 구성 요소가 있거든요.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: There are air route traffic control centers. There's 22 of those. They handle the high altitude traffic. There are regional facilities that manage the flow towards airports and away from airports,
segments.ko: 전국에 22개의 항공로 교통 관제 센터가 있습니다. 고고도 교통을 담당하죠. 공항으로 들어오고 나가는 흐름을 관리하는 지역 시설들도 있고요.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: and then there's the towers of the airports themselves and the command center in Virginia. They are all connected by a network that needs to be able to transfer in real time information about where our planes are, what the traffic is,
segments.ko: 그리고 공항의 관제탑과 버지니아에 있는 지휘 센터가 있습니다. 이들은 모두 네트워크로 연결되어 비행기의 위치, 교통 상황 등의 정보를 실시간으로 전송할 수 있어야 합니다.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: and other data about whether and other inputs that are important for both the controllers and the pilots to make sure they are flying safely.
segments.ko: 그리고 기상 정보 등 관제사와 조종사가 안전하게 비행하는 데 필요한 다른 데이터들도 포함되죠.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: But when you start to have a router overload the system, when one facility or two facilities in this case start to just flood the system with too many data pings, with too many efforts to connect to a variety of different places that normally they might not be doing,
segments.ko: 하지만 라우터가 시스템에 과부하를 주기 시작할 때, 즉 이번처럼 한두 개 시설에서 너무 많은 데이터 핑을 보내고 평소라면 하지 않았을 여러 장소로의 연결 시도로 시스템을 마비시킬 때,
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: you start to basically crowd out the space and it becomes unreliable.
segments.ko: 기본적으로 공간을 꽉 채우기 시작하고 시스템을 신뢰할 수 없게 됩니다.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: And the net effect of that is basically if you're an air traffic controller who needs to see any one of many things in order to make the planes not come too close to each other, you're not going to be able to actually like see a map or see the weather or see the distance or any of that other data that's trying to get through.
segments.ko: 그 결과, 비행기들이 서로 너무 가까워지지 않게 여러 가지를 확인해야 하는 항공 관제사라면 지도나 날씨, 거리 등 전송되려고 하는 다른 어떤 데이터도 실제로 볼 수 없게 되는 겁니다.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: This was not a total blackout. Let's make that clear. But the issue was that it was becoming unreliable and they were not sure where they were going to have the next glitch or the next slow to load issue that they needed to be able to get it.
segments.ko: 완전한 정전은 아니었습니다. 그 점은 분명히 하죠. 하지만 문제는 시스템을 믿을 수 없게 되었다는 것이었고, 다음 결함이나 로딩 지연 문제가 어디서 발생할지 알 수 없었다는 점입니다.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: And because you really do need to be able to have that real time data flow, they figure, this isn't safe. We don't know what's going to be the next shoe to drop here.
segments.ko: 실시간 데이터 흐름이 정말로 필요하기 때문에 그들은 '이건 안전하지 않다, 다음에 또 어떤 일이 터질지 모른다'고 판단한 것이죠.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: And we've got to just shut it all down before it becomes an actual situation of trying to avoid a real life accident where lives would be at stake.

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.ko: 기본적으로 FAA가 어떤 정보를 받고 있고 어떤 정보를 받지 못하고 있는지 알 수 없었기 때문에 전국적인 운항 중단이 있었던 거군요.
segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: And so therefore the safest thing to do was to tell everybody, don't fly.

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: Yes, and look, for days after, I mean, it was several hours, a few hours that this ground stock was in place. But for days after that, you really had the whole airline industry struggling to recover

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: because they were crews that got stranded in certain places or timed out because they hadn't slept overnight. And that created real backups for people who were trying to travel.

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: Karoun, you had said earlier that we have a lot more questions and answers about what exactly caused the system to be overloaded. And I wonder we're nearly a week out at this point. What have we learned about what happened last weekend?

segments.en: Well, we've learned where things went wrong. Eldreiro, Arkansas, and Amarillo, Texas, a radio facility and radar facility.

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: We've learned that there was a single contractor that was working on this particular upgrade in Arkansas and that they were being physically supervised by an FAA technician through it.
segments.ko: 아칸소에서 이 특정 업그레이드 작업을 수행하던 계약업체가 하나 있었고, FAA 기술자가 현장에서 직접 감독했다는 사실도 알게 되었습니다.

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: I mean, we're talking about a different sort of a system, but a router's job is to take the flow of data that's coming in and make it available to other devices, other parts of the network potentially. And so there's a predictable flow.
segments.ko: 다른 종류의 시스템이긴 하지만, 라우터의 역할은 들어오는 데이터 흐름을 받아 다른 장치나 네트워크의 다른 부분으로 전달하는 것입니다. 그래서 예측 가능한 흐름이 있죠.
segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: And when the router does something that is not predictable, it becomes a potential situation where it's flooding a system.

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: And that apparently happened based on a configuration that the FAA says, neither they nor the contractor changed or set. I don't want to get too much into the technical details,

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: but they are at a loss right now still, and they don't know if that was human error or if that was faulty equipment or if there was something that went wrong with the way they did the installation.

segments.speaker: Karoun Demirjian

segments.en: And those are still all open questions, even though we're basically a week out from when it actually happened.

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: And from your reporting, have the authorities ruled that out in this particular case when we're talking about the ground stoppage?

segments.speaker: Dustin Voltz

segments.en: Certainly, when you talk about anomalous router pinging, that can resemble perhaps a cyber activity, and that is something that I think could lead people to believe certain things.
segments.ko: 분명히 비정상적인 라우터 핑에 대해 이야기할 때 그것은 아마도 사이버 활동과 비슷할 수 있고, 그것이 사람들에게 어떤 추측을 하게 만들 수 있다고 생각합니다.
segments.speaker: Dustin Voltz

segments.en: But a numerous senior administration officials on the record in public in televised briefings and folks that I'm talking to in these agencies who are not speaking on the record, are saying the same thing that they don't think there's any evidence that that is what's going on here.

segments.speaker: Dustin Voltz
